summary: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Mysore, Queen's College, Benares, and under several teachers, including Ramamohana Brahmachari. He held posts at Maharaja's Sanskrit College (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (~1952).

Tissa Rajapatirana is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University (1966-1974) under Jan Willem de Jong and later held an attested post there in 1988.
Tiziana Pontillo is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.
Todd Gibson is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Indiana University under György Kara, where his PhD was attested in 1991.

Todd Thornton Lewis works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under mentors including Ainslie T. Embree, Morton Klass, and Alex Wayman, and held posts at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 1996, 2016-2017).

Tokan Tada was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Akita Prefectural Akita High School and Sera Monastery (1913-1923), and held posts at the University of Tokyo (1924), Tohoku University (1925), and Toyo Bunko (1956).
Toke Lindegaard Knudsen studied under Kim Plofker and David Pingree (2008).

Tokio Takata is a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS, holding posts at Otaru University of Commerce (1981-1983), Kyoto University (1983-2014), and Fudan University (2016-2022).

Tokugen Sakai was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and under Kodo Sawaki (1941), later serving as professor at Komazawa University (1949-1987) and lecturer at Eihei-ji (1977-1987).

Tokuno Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjirō Takakusu, holding posts at Fukui Prefectural Normal School (1879), Fukui Chugakko (1879-1882), and Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Freiburg under Kitarō Nishida, Edmund Husserl, and Martin Heidegger. His appointments included Kyoto University, Hitotsubashi University, and Ryukoku University.

Tom Tillemans is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied under Jacques May. He served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987-2018) and held a visiting chair at the University of Calgary.

Tomoko Masuzawa specializes in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale University (MA 1979), and UC Santa Barbara (PhD 1985), holding posts at UNC Chapel Hill (~1987-2000) and the University of Michigan (1999).
Tomoyasu Oshima specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Toshifumi Goto and held a part-time lecturer post at Kyoto University attested in 2012.
Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and held an attested post there as a lecturer in 2015.

Tomoyuki Uno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 1998) and served as associate professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000-2006).

Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Madras and Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal and C. S. Sundaram, holding a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison and William Sax, and held posts at Canterbury (attested 1990), Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000), and the University of Berlin (attested 2006-2009).

Tony K. Stewart is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Western Kentucky University. He held academic posts at North Carolina State University (~1986-2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011).

Torakazu Doi was a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe (~1922-1925) and later held posts at Sagami Women's University and Dokkyo University (~1964-1971).
